newsitem.title: CANADA: ALPINE SKIING-CHAMPION SEIZINGER WINS WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-CHAMPION SEIZINGER WINS WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.

text.p: Defending women's World Cup overall champion Katja Seizinger of Germany, who started the week complaining, was smiling, a little, after winning the first women's downhill of the season Saturday.
"Winning always feels good," Seizinger said after triumphing by an impressive six-tenths of a second.
Picking up speed down the course, she finished in 1 minute, 41.91 seconds. Carole Montillet of France was second in 1:42.51 and Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden third in 1:42.64.

Seizinger, who won a super-giant slalom at Lake Louise two years ago and was second in two downhills in the past two seasons here, took charge at the top of the 2.8-kilometre run and kept adding to her lead under an overcast sky and 14-degree Fahrenheit (minus 10 Celsius) weather.
The win was the 26th of her career and 12th in downhill.

"This is a good start for my season. It gives me confidence for the next downhill," said the 24-year-old, who bolted from the finish area and disappeared for a while after the race. Later, she explained she had gone to get her skis for super-G training.
The second downhill of the season is next week in Vail, Colorado. The super-G is on Sunday.
Seizinger won the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden, Austria, and has 260 points after four races, putting her more than 100 points ahead of the pack in the overall points standings.

At the start of the week, after winning the first official training run, Seizinger muttered about being at a disadvantage against downhill specialists because she didn't have enough time to train for the speed events.
But on Saturday, she said she felt better, although she did not expect to win by such a wide margin. "I thought it would be close, so this big difference surprises me."
"I'm a little surprised by my result," Montillet said. "I didn't expect to ski so well. I had some trouble with ice on the course."
Picabo Street, the American who has won at Lake Louise each of the last two seasons and captured the World Cup downhill crown each winter, finished fourth with a time of 1:42.68.
"That's great for me. I made a couple of mistakes but I know what I have to clean-up before Vail and I'm ready for the super-G," Street said.
Seizinger started 17th in the field of 55 racers and Wiberg skied 28th. Street said she and Wiberg, nicknamed "Pila," knew Seizinger had a strong run but felt they still had a chance.

"Pila and I were up at the start and we heard about Seizie's time but then the sun came out for a little bit and we both smiled -- we thought that might speed up the course for us," said Street. "But we couldn't catch Katja. She really nailed the course."
